newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to qualify for EMU, Waigel writes.
newsitem.headline: Germany to qualify for EMU, Waigel writes.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel wrote in an article published on Wednesday that Germany would cut its budget deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product this year and thus qualify for European monetary union.
Waigel, commenting on the recent G7 meeting in Washington, also said the normalisation of currency values on foreign exchange markets was now complete and would help the German economy.
"The budget deficit this year will be 2.9 percent of gross domestic product," Waigel wrote in the Bayernkurier, his Christian Social Union (CSU) party's newspaper.
Waigel also said: "The normalisation of exchange rates which has now been completed will contribute to supporting the economy."

"Normalisation" is G7-speak for gains by the U.S. dollar against the deutschemark and other leading currencies. The greenback rallied after the G7 meeting to 1.7395 marks, its highest since February 1994, before falling back.
Waigel noted that the International Monetary Fund had forecast an acceleration in the pace of economic growth in leading industrial countries.

But that would not be enough to fight high unemployment, which Waigel said could only be combatted with structural reforms. The IMF considers 80 percent of joblessness in Germany to be structural, not cyclical, he said.
Waigel called on pay bargainers to show moderation. He added that his plans to pass up to 30 billion marks in tax reforms would strengthen Germany as a place to do business.
